summary.en: The Byzantine Empire was the eastern continuation of the Roman Empire, with Constantinople as its capital. It survived the fall of the West in the 5th century and lasted until 1453. The name Byzantium came only after the end of the empire; the inhabitants themselves called their empire Roman and themselves Romans.

text.en: There is no agreement on when the Byzantine Empire began. Often 330 is given, when Constantine the Great inaugurated Constantinople as the new capital in the east. Others count from 395, when the empire was divided after the death of Theodosius I, and some scholars place the beginning only in the 7th or 8th century.
On 29 May 1453 the Ottomans conquered Constantinople. The last emperor, Constantine XI, fell in the fighting, and the empire ceased to exist.
Constantinople, present-day Istanbul, throughout the empire's existence. The city was sacked by the Fourth Crusade in 1204 and retaken in 1261.

Justinian I (527–565), when the empire was at its largest, Heraclius (610–641), Basil II (976–1025), Alexios I Komnenos (1081–1118), Michael VIII (1261–1282), who retook Constantinople, and Constantine XI (1449–1453).

The double-headed eagle is the emblem most often associated with Byzantium. As an ornament it is found in Byzantine art from the 10th and 11th centuries, but together with the emperor it is securely attested only in 1301, under Andronikos II Palaiologos. In the empire's last centuries the imperial family wore it on clothing and equipment. The map nevertheless shows it for the whole of the empire's existence, as a symbol of the empire.

mapNote.en: In the map data the empire is called the Byzantine Empire from 633. The years 395–632 are shown as the Eastern Roman Empire, with Rome's symbol.

summary.en: The Kingdom of Cusco was the small city-state of the Incas around the city of Cusco in the Andes, in present-day Peru. The Inca Empire grew out of it.

text.en: According to tradition Manco Cápac organised the kingdom around the year 1200. The story of the founding belongs to Inca mythology, and all regnal years are approximate.
Around 1438 Cusi Yupanqui (Pachacuti) defeated the Chanka people, and the kingdom grew into the Inca Empire. The date is approximate.

mapNote.en: The sources differ: Wikipedia gives about 1200–about 1438 and Wikidata 1197–1438. The map shows the kingdom in 1294–1439, as in Cliopatria, with the same area throughout. The city of Cusco lies about 7 km outside the eastern edge of the area. The border is Cliopatria's estimate and not a known state border. From 1440 the map shows the Inca Empire.

summary.en: Italian East Africa was an Italian colony in the Horn of Africa in 1936–1941. Mussolini proclaimed it on 1 June 1936, after the conquest of Ethiopia in the Second Italo-Ethiopian War, and it comprised Ethiopia, Eritrea and Italian Somaliland. The capital was Addis Ababa.

mapNote.en: The sources give 1936–1941 (Wikidata), from 1 June 1936 to the Battle of Gondar in November 1941 (Wikipedia). The map shows the colony in 1936–1941 with Cliopatria’s borders: in 1940 also British Somaliland, which Italy took in August 1940, and in 1941 only the area around Gondar, because Cliopatria draws the rest of Ethiopia, Eritrea and Somaliland as the British Empire that year. Ethiopia does not appear as a country of its own on the map in 1936–1941: in 1936–1940 because it was conquered, and in 1941 because Cliopatria draws the country as the British Empire, although Haile Selassie returned to Addis Ababa on 5 May 1941 and was restored to the throne. The country regained full sovereignty in 1944. The Ethiopian Empire is shown until 1935 and again from 1942. The map follows Cliopatria here; the decision to draw the recognised state during an occupation applies only to the period after 1945.

note.en: Dingane founded his royal kraal here in 1829, the year after he took power by murdering Shaka. The source does not say when it ceased to be the capital; here it is shown until the end of his reign in 1840. Shaka's capital kwaBulawayo (founded around 1820) is not shown, because its location lacks coordinates in Wikidata.
Cetshwayo founded Ulundi when he became king in 1873. The British took it and razed it to the ground at the Battle of Ulundi on 4 July 1879.

The city was called La Plata when it became the provisional capital in 1826 and was named Sucre in 1839. Sucre is the capital according to the constitution, but the government and parliament have sat in La Paz since the early 20th century.

summary.en: Siam was the international name of the kingdom in present-day Thailand. English Wikipedia calls the period 1782–1932 the Rattanakosin Kingdom, after the new capital Bangkok, and says that after 1855 it was also called the Kingdom of Siam. Siam was the only country in Southeast Asia that kept its independence from the colonial powers Britain and France.

text.en: Rama I, the first king of the Chakri dynasty, moved the capital from Thonburi to the east bank of the Chao Phraya River, where Bangkok was built. The city’s official founding date is 21 April 1782.

In 1893 France sent gunboats up to Bangkok, and Siam ceded all of Laos east of the Mekong to French Indochina. In 1907 Siam ceded northwestern Cambodia with Battambang and Siem Reap to France, and in 1909 the northern Malay sultanates of Kedah, Kelantan, Terengganu and Perlis to British Malaya.
On 24 June 1932 the Bangkok garrison mutinied and seized power, led by a group of 49 officers, the Khana Ratsadon. The absolute monarchy was replaced by a constitutional monarchy.
King Vajiravudh introduced the tricolour flag in September 1917, because the earlier elephant flag was difficult to print. The map shows it from 1917.

mapNote.en: The sources give 1782–24 June 1932 (Wikipedia and Wikidata). The map shows Siam in 1783–1931, as in Cliopatria. The map calls the country Thailand from 1932, but according to Swedish Wikipedia the country was renamed Thailand only on 24 June 1939. The country was called Siam again from 1945 and Thailand again from 1949 (according to some sources 1948), so the map’s Thailand also covers the years 1945–1949.

summary.en: The Kingdom of Yemen was a monarchy in the north-western part of present-day Yemen. Imam Yahya took power in Sanaa in 1918, when the Ottoman Empire withdrew after the First World War. The capital was Sanaa until 1948 and then Taiz until 1962. Yemen became a member of the UN on 30 September 1947. A republican coup in 1962 led to civil war, and the royalists held only the northern part of the country until a peace deal in 1970.

mapNote.en: Wikidata gives 30 October 1918–1 December 1970. The map shows the kingdom in 1919–1961 and the Yemen Arab Republic from 1962: Cliopatria has a single entry for North Yemen in 1919–1989, which the map divides at the revolution of 1962. The map does not show that the royalists held the northern part of the country during the civil war of 1962–1970.

summary.en: The Yemen Arab Republic, often called North Yemen, was proclaimed in 1962 when officers overthrew the monarchy in Sanaa. The coup led to an eight-year civil war, which the republicans won. The capital was Sanaa. On 22 May 1990 the country united with South Yemen to form the present Republic of Yemen.

mapNote.en: Wikidata gives 26 September 1962–22 May 1990. The map shows the republic in 1962–1989, as in Cliopatria's entry for North Yemen, and the Republic of Yemen from 1990.

summary.en: South Yemen, the People's Democratic Republic of Yemen, grew out of the British Colony of Aden and the Aden Protectorate. After an armed rebellion against British rule from 1963, the People's Republic of Southern Yemen was proclaimed on 30 November 1967. The country was the only communist state in the Arab world and had Aden as its capital. On 22 May 1990 it united with North Yemen.

mapNote.en: The sources give 1967–1990 (Wikidata 30 November 1967–22 May 1990). The map shows the country in 1969–1989, as in Cliopatria; in 1967–1968 Cliopatria counts the area as part of the British Empire.

summary.en: Rhodesia was an unrecognised state in Southern Africa in 1965–1979. The white minority government of the British colony of Southern Rhodesia unilaterally declared independence from the United Kingdom on 11 November 1965 to delay rule by the black majority. The UN Security Council called on all states not to recognise the country (Resolution 216). Two African nationalist parties, ZAPU and ZANU, waged an armed insurgency, the Rhodesian Bush War. The capital was Salisbury, now Harare.

mapNote.en: The sources give 1965–1979 (Wikidata 11 November 1965–1 June 1979). The map shows Rhodesia in 1967–1978, as in Cliopatria, which counts the country as part of the British Empire in 1965–1966 and also in 1967–1968; in the latter two years the map shows only Rhodesia. Rhodesia was never recognised, but the map shows the country as Cliopatria does, by decision of Historia-globen.

summary.en: Zimbabwe Rhodesia was the name of the country from 1 June 1979, after elections and a transitional government in which Abel Muzorewa succeeded Ian Smith. Zimbabwe Rhodesia was not recognised by other countries either. In December 1979 the parties agreed that the country would revert to being a British colony pending new elections, and on 18 April 1980 it became independent as Zimbabwe.

mapNote.en: The sources differ: Wikipedia gives 1 June 1979–18 April 1980 and Wikidata 1 June–12 December 1979. Cliopatria has Zimbabwe Rhodesia in 1979–1982. The map shows Zimbabwe Rhodesia in 1979 and Zimbabwe from 1980, as Wikidata and Wikipedia do, with Cliopatria's border for Zimbabwe Rhodesia, which is the same as Zimbabwe's border in 1983.

summary.en: The Sultanate of Muscat and Oman was in practice under British protection. It arose in 1856, when the Omani Empire was divided after the death of Sultan Said bin Sultan, and was ruled by the Al Busaid dynasty. After a palace coup on 23 July 1970 the sultan's son Qaboos bin Said took power and founded the present Sultanate of Oman.

mapNote.en: Wikidata gives 1820–1970 and Wikipedia that the sultanate arose in 1856. The map shows Muscat and Oman in 1900–1955, as in Cliopatria, with one exception: Cliopatria has no entry for the country in 1947–1955, but an entry called Qatar Protectorate with exactly the same border as Muscat and Oman in 1946. The map shows that border as Muscat and Oman. From 1956 to 1972 Cliopatria counts the country as part of the British Empire.

summary.en: Surinam was a Dutch plantation colony from 1667, when Dutch forces captured the English colony during the Second Anglo-Dutch War. The plantations were worked by enslaved Africans; about 300,000 were taken to Surinam, and slavery was abolished in 1863. The British occupied the colony in 1799–1802 and 1804–1816. It remained a colony until 15 December 1954.

mapNote.en: The sources differ slightly: Wikipedia gives 1667–15 December 1954 and Wikidata 1667–14 December 1954. The map shows the colony in 1820–1954. Cliopatria counts Suriname in 1820–1975 as part of its entry Netherlands Antilles, whose mainland part has the same border as Suriname in 1976 in Cliopatria; the map shows Suriname with that border. In the years before 1820 Cliopatria counts Suriname as part of other entries.

summary.en: Through the Charter for the Kingdom of the Netherlands of 15 December 1954, Suriname became a country within the Kingdom, on an equal footing with the Netherlands and the Netherlands Antilles. The Netherlands kept responsibility for defence and foreign affairs. After negotiations with the Dutch government, Suriname became independent on 25 November 1975.

mapNote.en: The sources differ slightly: Wikipedia gives 15 December 1954 and Wikidata 29 December 1954 as the start; both give independence on 25 November 1975. The map shows the country in 1955–1975. Cliopatria counts Suriname in 1820–1975 as part of its entry Netherlands Antilles, whose mainland part has the same border as Suriname in 1976 in Cliopatria; the map shows Suriname with that border.

summary.en: The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was formed by Serbia and Montenegro on 27 April 1992, when the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia broke up. The UN did not accept it as the continuation of the old state (Security Council Resolution 777), and it was not allowed to join the UN. During the Yugoslav Wars and the Kosovo War the country was hit by economic sanctions. In February 2003 the federation was reconstituted as the state union of Serbia and Montenegro.

mapNote.en: Wikidata gives 27 April 1992–4 February 2003. Cliopatria calls the state Serbia-Montenegro in 1992–2005 and in 1992–1995 also counts the Republic of Serbian Krajina in Croatia and large parts of Bosnia and Herzegovina as part of it. The map instead shows the state with its own 1996 border from Cliopatria in 1992–1995 as well, and those areas as part of Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina, by decision of Historia-globen to show the internationally recognised state in times of war and occupation. From 2000 Kosovo is not included in Cliopatria's border.

summary.en: The state union of Serbia and Montenegro replaced the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia in February 2003. Montenegro left the union in June 2006, after which Serbia proclaimed its independence.

mapNote.en: Wikidata gives 2003–4 June 2006. The map shows the state union in 2003–2005 and Serbia and Montenegro as separate countries from 2006, as in Cliopatria.

summary.en: Albania declared its independence from the Ottoman Empire in Vlorë on 28 November 1912. The Principality of Albania (1914–1925) was formed after the Treaty of London and survived invasions during the First World War. In 1925 the monarchy was abolished and a republic was proclaimed. When Italy invaded the country in 1939 it was ruled by King Zog I, who went into exile in Greece, and Albania became an Italian protectorate.

mapNote.en: Wikidata gives 28 November 1912 as the start, the same year as the map. The map follows Cliopatria: in 1916–1919 it shows only the southern part of the country, because Cliopatria counts the rest as part of other empires (Tirana as part of Austria-Hungary in 1916–1918 and of Italy in 1919), and in 1939–1943 Cliopatria counts the country as part of Italy. From 1944 the map shows Albania again and from 1946 the People's Republic.

summary.en: The People's Socialist Republic of Albania was the communist state in Albania from 11 January 1946 to 29 April 1991. Until 1976 it was called the People's Republic of Albania. The Party of Labour of Albania had a monopoly on power, and the country was led by Enver Hoxha in 1946–1985 and then by Ramiz Alia. Albania broke with the Soviet Union and in 1978 also with China, declared itself the world's first explicitly atheist state in 1967 and left the Warsaw Pact after the invasion of Czechoslovakia in 1968.

mapNote.en: The sources differ: Wikipedia gives 11 January 1946–29 April 1991 and Wikidata 11 January 1946–22 March 1992. The map shows the People's Republic in 1946–1990 and the Republic of Albania from 1991, as in Cliopatria.
